titel: PlayStation Says Buying Isn’t Owning - WAN Show September 4, 2026

faehigkeiten.grund: Auslieferung wird je Abruf neu zusammengesetzt (megaphone vergibt je Abruf eine request_event_id, megaphone haengt ein timetoken an, Adresse traegt eine session_id, kein ETag und Cache-Control "max-age=0, no-cache, no-store", Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst megaphone.fm) - Byte-Offsets veralten (bei dynamischer Auslieferung sofort, gemessen 19.08.2026) und die Zeitachse verschiebt sich mit (eine Folge war 57 s kuerzer als 3,5 h zuvor), deshalb sind auch Sprungmarken in Sekunden unsicher

einzeiler: Sony fights a digital ownership lawsuit, Markiplier buys into GoPro, and Valve's servers…
kurzfassung: The hosts discuss a class-action lawsuit where Sony argues that digital game purchases are merely licenses rather than actual ownership. They also cover Markiplier accidentally becoming GoPro's largest investor ahead of a major corporate merger and a massive leak of early Valve server data. Additionally, they explore news regarding robot vacuum surveillance, YouTube's updated view-counting metrics, and ongoing tech improvements.
stichpunkte: Sony claims in a class-action lawsuit response that digital game buyers never actually own their games.
A Taiwanese man is sentenced to prison after using his robot vacuum's camera to record his wife's affair.
Markiplier becomes GoPro's largest investor right before a massive optical firm acquisition causes the stock to skyrocket.
A massive 12 to 13-terabyte leak exposes early Valve source code, unreleased builds, and concept art from 2003 to 2013.
YouTube updates its view-counting metrics to register a view the moment a video begins playing across all formats.
SteamDB is acquired by Nexus Mods and its founder steps down due to burnout.
Xbox rolls out a disc-to-digital feature for insiders that allows players to convert physical discs of delisted games into digital licenses.

clips.hook: Sony argues digital game ownership is impossible
clips.text: Sony defends itself in a lawsuit by stating that digital purchases are clearly defined in terms of service as non-owned licenses, asserting that true digital ownership would be impossible.

clips.hook: Jail time for using a robot vacuum to catch cheating
clips.text: A Taiwanese court sentences a husband to five months in prison and fines him after his wife countersues him for illegally recording her infidelity using a smart robot vacuum.
The hosts review stock market data showing GoPro's share price surging by nearly 180 percent following its sudden acquisition by an optical photonics firm.

clips.hook: YouTube changes how views are counted
clips.text: YouTube updates its metrics to count a view the absolute second a video starts playing across all content formats, regardless of watch duration.

clips.hook: Over 12 terabytes of Valve server data leaked online
clips.text: A decade's worth of internal Valve server content and unreleased game builds from 2003 to 2013 leaks online due to an accidentally left-open server endpoint.
